source: Phase 41 (2026-10-18): original questions on the chapters of Beast Academy Levels 1-5 and the AoPS books, written by Claude Sonnet from our own chapter summaries (docs/question-bank-beast-academy.md) and solved blind by Claude Opus (Claude Code agents, not runAi: no ai_runs rows), code-checked by lintQuestion; "checked" questions await a platform admin. Algebra 14-22 and Introduction to Geometry added 2026-10-22 by the same pipeline.

notes.BA4.01: Text-only: no figures, so angle estimation and measuring with a protractor are not tested; clock-hand questions describe the hands in words. Quadrilaterals use the exclusive trapezoid definition only where "exactly one pair of parallel sides" is stated.
notes.BA4.02: Multiplication of whole numbers only. Missing-factor questions use small friendly numbers (reasoning by multiplication, not long division).
notes.BA4.03: All text-only; no figures needed. The difficulty 3 exponent puzzles (units-digit cycle, smallest multiple that is a square) are stretches, with the pattern given in the stem where it is not obvious.
notes.BA4.04: All text-only; no figures needed. Some difficulty 3 items (complement counting, overlaps) are stretches but stay within the chapter.
notes.BA4.05: Division of whole numbers only; no decimals or fractions. Remainder stories use whole-number answers. Divisibility questions cover 2, 3, 5, 9, 10 only.
notes.BA4.06: All logic puzzles are text-only. Truth-teller/liar puzzles state the rule in the stem or use it as the basic premise; each puzzle was checked by brute force (a program enumerated every possible assignment and confirmed exactly one answer).
notes.BA4.07: Text-only throughout. Divisibility questions use digit-sum and last-digit rules; a few prime/perfect-square items rely on 143=11x13, 187=11x17.
notes.BA4.08: Fractions are written in LaTeX; numeric answers are fractions or mixed numbers in any equivalent form (e.g. 9/12 for 3/4). Questions that ask for simplest form give choice options that are NOT equal to the key.
notes.BA4.09: Text-only; no figures used. Number-line ideas are described in words. Distances and elevations are all integers.
notes.BA4.10: Text-only; answers are fractions or mixed numbers (numeric keys given as a/b or w n/d, choices in LaTeX). Mixed numbers with unlike denominators are included under adding and subtracting.
notes.BA4.11: Tenths and hundredths only (no thousandths), as the summary says. Fraction-to-decimal conversions use denominators that scale to 10 or 100 (halves, fourths, fifths, twentieths, twenty-fifths).
notes.BA4.12: Probabilities are single-step and equally likely, as the summary says; the spinners, cubes and coins are all described in words. Two-coin and three-coin questions list the outcomes in the stem. A few harder ones (adding marbles, a marble set aside) stay inside the chapter's fractions-of-a-collection idea.

questions.stem: An angle measures $90^\circ$. What kind of angle is it?
questions.solution: An angle of exactly 90 degrees is a right angle.

solve.work: 90 degrees is exactly a right angle.

questions.stem: Which of these angles is acute?
questions.solution: An acute angle is smaller than 90 degrees. Only 35 degrees is smaller than 90.

solve.work: Acute means less than 90; only 35 qualifies.

questions.stem: How many degrees is a straight angle?
questions.solution: A straight angle is a straight line, which is 180 degrees.

solve.work: A straight angle is half a turn: 180.

questions.stem: Which of these angles is obtuse?
questions.solution: An obtuse angle is bigger than 90 degrees and smaller than 180 degrees. Only 135 degrees fits.

solve.work: Obtuse is between 90 and 180; 135 qualifies (180 is straight, 90 right, 45 acute).

questions.stem: Mia draws an angle of $72^\circ$. What kind of angle did she draw?
questions.solution: 72 is less than 90, so the angle is acute.

questions.stem: An angle opens out flat, like a straight line. How many degrees is it?
questions.solution: A flat, straight angle is 180 degrees.

questions.skill: Missing angles on a line, in a right angle and around a point
questions.stem: A right angle is split into two angles. One of them is $30^\circ$. How many degrees is the other one?
questions.solution: A right angle is 90 degrees. 90 - 30 = 60.

questions.stem: Two angles sit side by side on a straight line. One is $100^\circ$. How many degrees is the other angle?
questions.solution: A straight line is 180 degrees. 180 - 100 = 80.

solve.work: Angles on a straight line sum to 180: 180 - 100 = 80.

questions.skill: Missing angles on a line, in a right angle and around a point
questions.stem: How many degrees are in a full turn all the way around a point?
questions.solution: A full turn is 360 degrees.

questions.stem: Angles $a$ and $b$ together make a right angle. If $a = 25^\circ$, how many degrees is $b$?
questions.solution: The two angles add to 90 degrees. 90 - 25 = 65.

questions.stem: A triangle has angles of $60^\circ$ and $70^\circ$. How many degrees is the third angle?
questions.solution: The angles of a triangle add to 180 degrees. 60 + 70 = 130, and 180 - 130 = 50.

questions.stem: The three angles of any triangle add up to how many degrees?
questions.solution: The angles of every triangle add up to 180 degrees.

questions.stem: A triangle has a right angle and an angle of $35^\circ$. How many degrees is its third angle?
Two angles of a triangle are each $45^\circ$. How many degrees is the third angle?
Two angles of a triangle are $20^\circ$ and $80^\circ$. How many degrees is the third angle?
A triangle has three sides that are each 5 cm long. What kind of triangle is it?
questions.solution: A triangle whose three sides are all equal is equilateral.

questions.stem: A triangle has sides of 4 cm, 4 cm and 7 cm. What kind of triangle is it, by its sides?
questions.solution: Exactly two sides are equal, so it is isosceles.

solve.work: Two sides equal (4, 4), third different: isosceles.

questions.stem: What is the name for a triangle whose three sides are all different lengths?
questions.solution: A triangle with three different side lengths is scalene.

questions.stem: How many of the sides of an equilateral triangle are the same length?
questions.solution: In an equilateral triangle all 3 sides are equal.

questions.stem: A triangle has one right angle. What kind of triangle is it?
questions.solution: A triangle with one right angle is called a right triangle.

solve.work: A triangle with a right angle is a right triangle.

questions.stem: A triangle has angles of $50^\circ$, $60^\circ$ and $70^\circ$. What kind of triangle is it, by its angles?
questions.solution: All three angles are smaller than 90 degrees, so the triangle is acute.

questions.stem: A triangle has an angle of $120^\circ$. What kind of triangle is it, by its angles?
questions.solution: An angle of 120 degrees is obtuse, so the triangle is obtuse.

questions.skill: Angles of isosceles and equilateral triangles
questions.stem: How many degrees is each angle of an equilateral triangle?
questions.solution: The three angles are equal and add to 180 degrees. 180 / 3 = 60.

questions.skill: Angles of isosceles and equilateral triangles
questions.stem: An isosceles triangle has two angles of $50^\circ$. How many degrees is its third angle?
How many sides does a quadrilateral have?
questions.solution: A quadrilateral is a shape with 4 sides.

questions.stem: Which shape always has four equal sides and four right angles?
questions.solution: A square has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles. A rectangle need not have equal sides, and a rhombus need not have right angles.

solve.work: Four equal sides and four right angles is a square; a rhombus need not have right angles, a rectangle need not have equal sides.

questions.stem: A four-sided shape has four right angles. Its sides are 3 cm, 6 cm, 3 cm and 6 cm. What is it?
questions.solution: Four right angles with sides that are not all equal make a rectangle.

solve.work: Four right angles with sides 3, 6, 3, 6 (not all equal): rectangle.

questions.stem: Which shape has exactly one pair of parallel sides?
questions.solution: A trapezoid has exactly one pair of parallel sides. The other three shapes have two pairs.

solve.work: Exactly one pair of parallel sides: trapezoid (parallelogram, rectangle, square have two pairs).

questions.stem: How many right angles does a rectangle have?
questions.solution: All four corners of a rectangle are right angles.

questions.stem: Which of these shapes is a quadrilateral?
questions.solution: A quadrilateral has 4 sides. A trapezoid has 4; a triangle has 3, a pentagon 5 and a hexagon 6.

solve.work: A trapezoid has four sides; the others have 3, 6, 5.

questions.stem: A square has sides of 6 cm. What is its perimeter, in centimeters?
questions.solution: 4 sides of 6 cm: 4 x 6 = 24.

questions.stem: A rectangle is 7 cm long and 3 cm wide. What is its perimeter, in centimeters?
Which list has only acute angles?
questions.solution: An acute angle is less than 90 degrees. Only the list 20, 89, 45 has every angle below 90. The others contain 90, 91 or 100.

solve.work: 20, 89, 45 are all under 90; each other list contains 90, 91 or 100.

questions.stem: An angle is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight angle. Which could be its measure?
questions.solution: It must be between 90 and 180 degrees, not equal to either. Only 179 degrees fits.

questions.stem: Here are five angles: $15^\circ$, $90^\circ$, $100^\circ$, $45^\circ$ and $170^\circ$. How many of them are obtuse?
questions.solution: Obtuse angles are between 90 and 180 degrees. Only 100 and 170 are, so there are 2.

solve.work: Obtuse (90 < x < 180): 100 and 170. 90 is right. Count 2.

questions.solution: A full turn is 360 degrees. 360 / 4 = 90.

questions.stem: At 4:00 the hour hand points at the 4 and the minute hand points at the 12. The 12 numbers on a clock are spread evenly around a full turn. How many degrees is the angle between the hands?
questions.solution: Each gap between numbers is 360 / 12 = 30 degrees. From 12 to 4 is 4 gaps: 4 x 30 = 120 degrees.

solve.work: Each hour mark is 360/12 = 30 degrees. From 12 to 4 is 4 x 30 = 120.

questions.stem: Which of these could be the three angles of a triangle?
questions.solution: The angles must add to 180. 50 + 60 + 70 = 180. The others add to 190, 190 and 190.

questions.stem: A garden is shaped like a triangle. Two of its corners have angles of $48^\circ$ and $67^\circ$. How many degrees is the angle at the third corner?
In a triangle, one angle is $25^\circ$ and another angle is three times as big. How many degrees is the third angle?
questions.solution: The second angle is 3 x 25 = 75. Then 25 + 75 = 100, and 180 - 100 = 80.

questions.stem: A right triangle has one acute angle of $38^\circ$. How many degrees is its other acute angle?
questions.solution: The right angle is 90 degrees, so the two acute angles add to 90. 90 - 38 = 52.

questions.stem: Which set of angles can NOT be the three angles of a triangle?
questions.solution: The angles of a triangle add to 180. 90 + 90 + 10 = 190, which is too much. The other three sets each add to exactly 180.

solve.work: 90+90+10 = 190, not 180 (and two right angles impossible). The others each sum to 180.

questions.stem: Which set of side lengths makes an isosceles triangle (exactly two sides equal)?
questions.solution: Only 5, 5, 8 has exactly two equal sides. In the other sets all three sides are different.

solve.work: Only 5, 5, 8 has exactly two equal sides (valid: 5+5>8).

questions.stem: Which set of side lengths makes an equilateral triangle?
questions.solution: An equilateral triangle has all three sides equal, so 9, 9, 9.

questions.stem: An equilateral triangle has sides of 9 cm. What is its perimeter, in centimeters?
questions.solution: 3 sides of 9 cm: 3 x 9 = 27.

questions.stem: An isosceles triangle has two sides of 7 cm each, and its perimeter is 20 cm. How long is the third side, in centimeters?
A triangle has sides of 5 cm, 7 cm and 9 cm. Which word describes it, by its sides?
questions.solution: All three sides are different lengths, so it is scalene.

questions.stem: A triangle has angles of $35^\circ$ and $55^\circ$. What kind of triangle is it, by its angles?
questions.solution: The third angle is 180 - 35 - 55 = 90 degrees, so it is a right triangle.

questions.stem: Two angles of a triangle are $40^\circ$ and $45^\circ$. What kind of triangle is it, by its angles?
questions.solution: The third angle is 180 - 40 - 45 = 95 degrees, which is obtuse. So the triangle is obtuse.

questions.solution: The third angle is 180 - 75 - 80 = 25 degrees. All three angles (75, 80, 25) are below 90, so the triangle is acute.

solve.work: Third angle 180 - 75 - 80 = 25; all angles 75, 80, 25 under 90: acute.

No, because the two right angles already add to $180^\circ$
Yes, if all three sides are equal
No, because a triangle cannot have any right angle
questions.answer: No, because the two right angles already add to $180^\circ$

solve.answer: No, because the two right angles already add to $180^\circ$
solve.work: Two right angles total 180, leaving 0 for the third angle, so no.

questions.solution: 180 - 40 = 140, shared by two equal angles: 140 / 2 = 70.

questions.skill: Angles of isosceles and equilateral triangles
questions.stem: An isosceles triangle has two equal base angles of $65^\circ$ each. How many degrees is its top angle?

questions.skill: Angles of isosceles and equilateral triangles
questions.stem: A right triangle has two sides of equal length. How many degrees is each of its acute angles?
questions.solution: The two equal sides have equal angles opposite them. The acute angles add to 90, so each is 90 / 2 = 45.

solve.work: Right isosceles: the two acute angles are equal, (180 - 90)/2 = 45.

questions.skill: Angles of isosceles and equilateral triangles
questions.stem: Two angles of a triangle are equal. The third angle is $30^\circ$. How many degrees is each of the equal angles?
Which statement is true?
choices: Every rhombus has four right angles.
questions.solution: A square has four right angles, so it is a rectangle. But a rectangle can have unequal sides, and a rhombus can lean over, so the other statements are false.

solve.work: A square has four right angles and two pairs of equal opposite sides, so every square is a rectangle. Others false.

questions.stem: A four-sided shape has four equal sides. Its angles are $60^\circ$, $120^\circ$, $60^\circ$ and $120^\circ$. What is it?
questions.solution: Four equal sides with no right angles make a rhombus. It is not a square or rectangle because it has no right angles.

solve.work: Four equal sides, angles not right: rhombus.

questions.stem: How many pairs of parallel sides does a parallelogram have?
questions.solution: A parallelogram has two pairs of parallel sides: the top and bottom, and the two slanted sides.

solve.work: A parallelogram has 2 pairs of parallel sides.

questions.stem: A quadrilateral has two pairs of parallel sides. Two sides are 4 cm and two sides are 7 cm. It has no right angles. What is it?
questions.solution: Two pairs of parallel sides make a parallelogram. With no right angles it is not a rectangle or square, and the unequal sides rule out a rhombus.

solve.work: Two pairs of parallel sides, sides 4 and 7 (not all equal), no right angles: parallelogram.

questions.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 40 cm and is 12 cm long. How wide is it, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Half of the perimeter is length + width = 20. So the width is 20 - 12 = 8.

questions.stem: A trapezoid has sides of 5 cm, 9 cm, 4 cm and 6 cm. What is its perimeter, in centimeters?

solve.work: 5 + 9 + 4 + 6 = 24 (such a trapezoid exists, e.g. bases 9 and 5 with legs 4 and 6).

questions.stem: An angle is obtuse and its measure is a multiple of 20 degrees. What is the smallest it could be, in degrees?
questions.solution: Multiples of 20 are 20, 40, 60, 80, 100. The first one over 90 is 100.

solve.work: Obtuse: more than 90, less than 180. Multiples of 20 above 90: 100 is the smallest.

questions.stem: How many whole-number degree measures are obtuse angles that are less than $100^\circ$?
questions.solution: Obtuse means more than 90. The whole numbers from 91 to 99 are 9 numbers.

questions.stem: Two acute angles are put side by side to make one bigger angle. Which kind of angle can NEVER be made this way?
questions.solution: Two acute angles add to less than 90 + 90 = 180, so they can never make exactly 180 (a straight angle). They can make acute, right or obtuse angles, for example 20 + 30, 45 + 45 and 80 + 80.

solve.work: Two acute angles total less than 90 + 90 = 180, so never straight. Right (45+45), obtuse (80+80), acute (20+30) are all possible.

questions.skill: Missing angles on a line, in a right angle and around a point
questions.stem: Two angles lie on a straight line. One is $20^\circ$ bigger than the other. How many degrees is the smaller angle?
questions.solution: If the angles were equal they would be 90 each. Take away the extra 20: 180 - 20 = 160, and 160 / 2 = 80. The angles are 80 and 100.

questions.skill: Missing angles on a line, in a right angle and around a point
questions.stem: Two angles together make a right angle, and one is twice as big as the other. How many degrees is the smaller angle?
questions.solution: The angles are 1 part and 2 parts, 3 parts in all. 90 / 3 = 30 degrees per part, so the smaller angle is 30.

questions.skill: Missing angles on a line, in a right angle and around a point
questions.stem: Two angles lie on a straight line. One is four times as big as the other. How many degrees is the larger angle?
questions.solution: There are 1 + 4 = 5 equal parts in 180 degrees. Each part is 36, so the larger angle is 4 x 36 = 144.

questions.skill: Missing angles on a line, in a right angle and around a point
questions.stem: A straight angle is cut into three angles. The second angle is twice the first and the third is three times the first. How many degrees is the first angle?
questions.solution: In parts: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 parts make 180 degrees, so one part is 30.

questions.skill: Missing angles on a line, in a right angle and around a point
questions.stem: At 8:00 the hour hand points at the 8 and the minute hand points at the 12. The 12 numbers on a clock are spread evenly around a full turn. What is the smaller of the two angles between the hands, in degrees?
questions.solution: Each gap is 30 degrees. From 8 around to 12 is 4 gaps, which is 120 degrees. The other way round is 8 gaps, 240 degrees. The smaller is 120.

solve.work: From 12 clockwise to 8 is 8 x 30 = 240; the smaller angle is 360 - 240 = 120.

questions.skill: Missing angles on a line, in a right angle and around a point
questions.stem: Four angles fit exactly around a point. Three of them are equal and the fourth is $60^\circ$. How many degrees is each of the three equal angles?
questions.solution: 360 - 60 = 300, shared by three equal angles: 300 / 3 = 100.

questions.stem: The angles of a triangle are $x^\circ$, $2x^\circ$ and $3x^\circ$. What is the smallest angle?
questions.solution: x + 2x + 3x = 6x = 180, so x = 30. The smallest angle is 30 degrees.

questions.stem: The angles of a triangle are $a^\circ$, $(a + 20)^\circ$ and $(a + 40)^\circ$, where $a$ is a whole number. How many degrees is the largest angle?
questions.solution: Together: 3a + 60 = 180, so 3a = 120 and a = 40. The largest is 40 + 40 = 80.

questions.stem: Two angles of a triangle are $85^\circ$ and $86^\circ$. How many degrees is the third angle?
In a triangle, the middle-sized angle is $60^\circ$ and the largest angle is three times the smallest. How many degrees is the largest angle?
questions.solution: The smallest and largest angles add to 180 - 60 = 120. They are 1 part and 3 parts, 4 parts in all, so one part is 30. The largest is 3 x 30 = 90.

solve.work: Smallest s, largest 3s: s + 60 + 3s = 180, 4s = 120, s = 30; angles 30, 60, 90 (60 is indeed the middle). Largest 90.

questions.stem: A student says a triangle has angles of $64^\circ$, $58^\circ$ and $62^\circ$. By how many degrees do these three angles miss the correct total for a triangle?
questions.solution: 64 + 58 + 62 = 184, but a triangle's angles add to 180. They miss by 4 degrees.

questions.stem: A triangle has angles of $a^\circ$ and $b^\circ$. Which expression gives its third angle, in degrees?
questions.solution: The three angles add to 180, so the third angle is 180 minus the other two: 180 - a - b.

questions.stem: An isosceles triangle has a perimeter of 29 cm and a base of 11 cm. The other two sides are equal. How long is each of them, in centimeters?
questions.solution: 29 - 11 = 18, shared by two equal sides: 18 / 2 = 9.

questions.stem: An equilateral triangle has a perimeter of 36 cm. A second equilateral triangle has sides that are each 3 cm shorter. What is the second triangle's perimeter, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The first triangle has sides of 36 / 3 = 12 cm. The second has sides of 9 cm, so its perimeter is 3 x 9 = 27.

questions.stem: Here are five triangles, with side lengths in cm: (3, 3, 5), (4, 5, 6), (7, 7, 2), (6, 6, 6), (2, 8, 8). How many of them have exactly two equal sides?
questions.solution: (3, 3, 5), (7, 7, 2) and (2, 8, 8) each have exactly two equal sides. (4, 5, 6) has none and (6, 6, 6) has three. So there are 3.

solve.work: (3,3,5) yes; (4,5,6) no; (7,7,2) yes; (6,6,6) no, all three equal; (2,8,8) yes. Count 3.

questions.stem: A triangle has a perimeter of 24 cm, and two of its sides are 8 cm each. By its sides, what kind of triangle must it be?
questions.solution: 8 + 8 = 16, so the third side is 24 - 16 = 8 cm. All three sides are 8 cm, so it is equilateral.

solve.work: Third side 24 - 16 = 8, so all sides 8: equilateral.

questions.stem: What is the smallest number of acute angles that any triangle can have?
questions.solution: A triangle's angles add to 180, so two angles that are 90 or more would already use up 180. So at least two angles must be acute.

solve.work: At most one angle can be 90 or more, so every triangle has at least 2 acute angles; e.g. a right triangle has exactly 2.

questions.stem: The angles of a triangle are $x^\circ$, $x^\circ$ and $2x^\circ$. What kind of triangle is it, by its angles?
questions.solution: x + x + 2x = 4x = 180, so x = 45. The angles are 45, 45 and 90, which makes a right triangle.

questions.stem: One angle of a triangle is $100^\circ$. Which statement must be true?
choices: The other two angles add to $100^\circ$.
The other two angles are both acute.
The other two angles are equal.
questions.answer: The other two angles are both acute.
questions.solution: The other two angles add to 180 - 100 = 80 degrees, so each is less than 80 and therefore acute. They need not be equal, and they do not add to 100.

solve.answer: The other two angles are both acute.
solve.work: Other two add to 80, so each is less than 80: both acute. Not necessarily equal/isosceles; they add to 80 not 100.

questions.stem: Here are five sets of angles: (20, 30, 130), (60, 60, 60), (100, 40, 40), (90, 45, 45), (10, 10, 160). How many of them are the angles of an obtuse triangle?
questions.solution: Each set adds to 180. An obtuse triangle has one angle over 90: (20, 30, 130), (100, 40, 40) and (10, 10, 160). That is 3.

questions.skill: Angles of isosceles and equilateral triangles
questions.stem: An isosceles triangle has an angle of $100^\circ$, and its other two angles are equal. How many degrees is each of the other two angles?
questions.solution: 180 - 100 = 80, shared by two equal angles: 80 / 2 = 40.

questions.skill: Angles of isosceles and equilateral triangles
questions.stem: The top angle of an isosceles triangle is three times as big as each of its two equal base angles. How many degrees is the top angle?
questions.solution: In parts: the top is 3 parts and each base angle 1 part, 5 parts in all. 180 / 5 = 36, so the top angle is 3 x 36 = 108.

questions.skill: Angles of isosceles and equilateral triangles
questions.stem: Two identical equilateral triangles share one side to make a four-sided shape. How many degrees is the biggest angle of the new shape?
questions.solution: Two of the shape's corners are made from two triangle angles side by side: 60 + 60 = 120. The other two corners are 60 each. So the biggest is 120.

solve.work: The shape is a rhombus with angles 60, 120, 60, 120 (the shared-side ends get 60 + 60). Biggest 120.

questions.skill: Angles of isosceles and equilateral triangles
questions.stem: In an isosceles triangle, each of the two equal base angles is $15^\circ$ bigger than the top angle. How many degrees is the top angle?
questions.solution: If the top angle is t, the base angles are t + 15 each. So 3t + 30 = 180, 3t = 150 and t = 50.

questions.stem: Which shape has four equal sides AND four equal angles?
questions.solution: Four equal angles make each one 90 degrees, so a rectangle; adding four equal sides gives a square. A rhombus has equal sides but not always equal angles; a rectangle has equal angles but not always equal sides.

solve.work: Four equal sides and four equal angles: square.

questions.stem: A square is cut along one diagonal into two triangles. How many degrees is each acute angle of these triangles?
questions.solution: The diagonal cuts a 90 degree corner into two equal angles: 90 / 2 = 45.

solve.work: The diagonal bisects the right angles: 90/2 = 45.

questions.stem: A rectangle is cut along a diagonal into two triangles. In one of the triangles, the two angles that are not the right angle add up to how many degrees?
questions.solution: A triangle's angles add to 180 and one of them is 90, so the other two add to 180 - 90 = 90.

questions.stem: Which statement is FALSE?
choices: A rectangle has two pairs of equal sides.
questions.solution: A rhombus has four equal sides but may have no right angles, so it need not be a square. The other three statements are true.

solve.work: A rhombus need not have right angles, so "Every rhombus is a square" is false. The others are true.

questions.stem: A square has the same perimeter as a rectangle that is 10 cm long and 6 cm wide. How long is a side of the square?
questions.solution: The rectangle's perimeter is 2 x (10 + 6) = 32 cm. A square with perimeter 32 has sides of 32 / 4 = 8 cm.

solve.work: Rectangle perimeter 2 x (10 + 6) = 32; square side 32/4 = 8 cm.

questions.stem: Two squares with sides of 5 cm are placed side by side to make one rectangle. What is the rectangle's perimeter, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The rectangle is 5 + 5 = 10 cm long and 5 cm wide. Perimeter: 10 + 5 + 10 + 5 = 30.

solve.work: The rectangle is 10 cm by 5 cm; perimeter 2 x 15 = 30.

questions.stem: Which counting number, when squared, is 20 more than the number itself?
questions.solution: Try numbers: $4^2 = 16$ is only 12 more than 4. $5^2 = 25$ is 20 more than 5. Larger numbers give a bigger gap, so the answer is 5.

questions.stem: Which of these is equal to $2^5 + 2^5$?
questions.solution: Two copies of $2^5$ make $2 \times 2^5 = 2^6$. In numbers, $32 + 32 = 64 = 2^6$.

questions.stem: How many two-digit numbers can you make using only the digits 1 and 2, if a digit may be used twice?
questions.solution: List them in order: 11, 12, 21, 22. There are 4.

questions.stem: Ann, Ben and Cal want to pick two of the three of them to carry a banner. How many different pairs can be picked?
questions.solution: List the pairs in order: Ann and Ben, Ann and Cal, Ben and Cal. There are 3 pairs.

questions.stem: A coin is flipped twice. H means heads and T means tails. Which list shows every possible result?
questions.solution: The first flip is H or T, and so is the second: HH, HT, TH, TT. That is 4 results, with none missing and none repeated.

solve.work: Ordered results: HH, HT, TH, TT.

questions.stem: How many ways can you make 5 cents using only pennies (1 cent each) and nickels (5 cents each)?
questions.solution: Either 5 pennies, or 1 nickel. That is 2 ways.

questions.stem: Write 4 as the sum of two counting numbers, such as 1 + 3. Count 1 + 3 and 3 + 1 as different. How many ways are there?
questions.solution: The ways are 1 + 3, 2 + 2 and 3 + 1. That is 3 ways.

questions.stem: List the whole numbers from 1 to 20 that have the digit 2 in them. How many numbers are on your list?
questions.solution: The numbers are 2, 12 and 20. That is 3 numbers.

questions.skill: How many numbers in a list
questions.stem: How many whole numbers are there from 5 to 12, counting both 5 and 12?
questions.solution: The numbers are 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12. Subtract and add 1: $12 - 5 + 1 = 8$.

questions.skill: How many numbers in a list
questions.stem: Houses on Oak Street are numbered from 31 to 40. How many houses are there?
questions.solution: Subtracting gives 9, but that leaves out one end. Count both ends: $40 - 31 + 1 = 10$ houses.

questions.skill: How many numbers in a list
questions.stem: Ben reads pages 20 through 29 of a book. How many pages does he read?

questions.skill: How many numbers in a list
questions.stem: How many numbers are in the list 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12?
questions.solution: Count them one by one: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 is 6 numbers.

questions.skill: How many numbers in a list
questions.stem: Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, and so on up to 50. How many numbers are in the list?
questions.solution: The numbers are 5 times 1, 5 times 2, up to 5 times 10. That is 10 numbers.

questions.skill: How many numbers in a list
questions.stem: How many whole numbers are between 10 and 20, not counting 10 or 20?
questions.solution: The numbers are 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19. That is 9 numbers.

questions.skill: How many numbers in a list
questions.stem: A camp lasts from March 3 to March 9, counting both days. How many days does the camp last?
Ava has 3 shirts and 2 hats. How many different shirt-and-hat outfits can she make?
questions.solution: Each of the 3 shirts can go with each of the 2 hats: $3 \times 2 = 6$ outfits.

questions.stem: A cafe sells 4 kinds of sandwich and 3 kinds of drink. How many ways are there to choose one sandwich and one drink?
questions.solution: Each of the 4 sandwiches goes with each of the 3 drinks: $4 \times 3 = 12$ ways. Adding (7) would only count the items.

questions.stem: A lock code is a letter, A or B, followed by a digit, 1, 2 or 3. How many different codes are there?
questions.solution: 2 choices for the letter and 3 for the digit: $2 \times 3 = 6$ codes.

questions.stem: There are 5 roads from Town A to Town B, and 2 roads from Town B to Town C. How many ways can you travel from A to C, going through B?
questions.solution: For each of the 5 roads to B there are 2 roads on to C: $5 \times 2 = 10$ ways.

questions.stem: A pizza shop offers 2 sizes and 3 toppings. A customer picks one size and one topping. How many different pizzas are possible?
questions.solution: Each size goes with each topping: $2 \times 3 = 6$ pizzas.

questions.stem: An ice-cream stand has 4 flavors and 2 kinds of cone. How many different one-scoop cones can you order?
questions.solution: Each flavor can go on each kind of cone: $4 \times 2 = 8$ cones.

questions.stem: A password is one digit from 0 to 9 followed by one of the letters A, B or C. How many passwords are possible?
questions.solution: There are 10 digits and 3 letters: $10 \times 3 = 30$ passwords.

questions.stem: A game has two spinners. One has 5 sections and the other has 3 sections. How many different pairs of results can come up?
questions.solution: Each of the 5 results of the first spinner pairs with each of the 3 results of the second: $5 \times 3 = 15$.

questions.stem: In how many different orders can 3 friends, Ann, Bo and Cy, stand in a line?
questions.solution: List them: ABC, ACB, BAC, BCA, CAB, CBA. That is 6 orders. (3 choices for first place, then 2, then 1.)

questions.stem: A code has 2 digits, and each digit can be any of 0 to 9. How many codes are there?
questions.solution: 10 choices for the first digit and 10 for the second: $10 \times 10 = 100$ codes (00 to 99).

questions.stem: Using only the digits 1, 2 and 3, how many 2-digit codes can be made if a digit may be repeated?
questions.solution: 3 choices for the first digit and 3 for the second: $3 \times 3 = 9$ codes.

questions.stem: A code is made of 2 different letters chosen from A, B and C, in order. How many codes are possible?
questions.solution: 3 choices for the first letter, then 2 left for the second: $3 \times 2 = 6$ codes: AB, AC, BA, BC, CA, CB.

solve.work: 3 x 2 = 6: AB, AC, BA, BC, CA, CB.

questions.stem: A gym locker has 3 dials, and each dial can show 0 or 1. How many different settings are there?
questions.solution: 2 choices for each of the 3 dials: $2 \times 2 \times 2 = 8$ settings.

questions.stem: A club has 4 members. They pick a president, and then a vice president who must be a different person. In how many ways can they do this?
questions.solution: 4 choices for president, then 3 people are left for vice president: $4 \times 3 = 12$ ways.

questions.stem: In a line of children, Mia is 3rd from the front and 4th from the back. How many children are in the line?
questions.solution: Adding 3 and 4 counts Mia twice. So $3 + 4 - 1 = 6$ children.

questions.stem: A teacher asks who has a brother and who has a sister. 5 children have a brother, 3 children have a sister, and none have both. How many children have a brother or a sister?
questions.solution: No child is in both groups, so nobody is counted twice: $5 + 3 = 8$ children.

questions.stem: On a team, 6 children play soccer, 5 play tennis and 2 play both. Which calculation counts the children who play at least one of the two sports without counting anyone twice?
questions.solution: The 2 who play both are counted once in the 6 and again in the 5, so take them away once: $6 + 5 - 2 = 9$.

questions.stem: Jo writes the list 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. Kim writes the list 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. How many different numbers are on the two lists together?
questions.solution: The numbers 1 to 9 all appear, and 5, 6 and 7 are on both lists. Together: 9 different numbers.

questions.stem: In a row of children, Tom is 5th from the left and 5th from the right. How many children are in the row?
questions.solution: Tom is counted in both 5s, so $5 + 5 - 1 = 9$ children.

questions.stem: Four children wear hats and three wear scarves. One child wears both a hat and a scarf. How many children wear a hat or a scarf?
questions.solution: The child with both is in both counts. $4 + 3 - 1 = 6$ children.

questions.stem: How many ways can you make 25 cents using only dimes (10 cents each) and nickels (5 cents each)?
questions.solution: With 0 dimes: 5 nickels. With 1 dime: 15 cents left, 3 nickels. With 2 dimes: 5 cents left, 1 nickel. That is 3 ways.

questions.stem: Each of the digits 2, 5 and 8 may be used at most once in a number. How many two-digit numbers can be made?
questions.solution: List them: 25, 28, 52, 58, 82, 85. That is 6 numbers.

questions.stem: How many different pairs of two letters can be chosen from A, B, C and D, if the pair AB and the pair BA count as the same?
questions.solution: List them in order: AB, AC, AD, BC, BD, CD. That is 6 pairs.

solve.work: AB, AC, AD, BC, BD, CD = 6.

questions.stem: A red die and a blue die are rolled. In how many ways can the two numbers add up to 5?
questions.solution: List (red, blue): (1, 4), (2, 3), (3, 2), (4, 1). That is 4 ways.

questions.stem: Sam climbs 4 stairs. With each step he goes up 1 stair or 2 stairs. In how many different ways can he reach the top?
questions.solution: List by steps: 1+1+1+1, 1+1+2, 1+2+1, 2+1+1 and 2+2. That is 5 ways.

questions.stem: Tia lists every arrangement of the letters A, B and C, using each letter once. So far she has ABC, ACB, BAC, BCA and CAB. Which arrangement is still missing?
questions.solution: There are 6 arrangements: ABC, ACB, BAC, BCA, CAB and CBA. Only CBA is not on her list.

questions.skill: How many numbers in a list
questions.stem: How many numbers are in the list 7, 8, 9, and so on up to 94?
questions.solution: Subtract and add 1: $94 - 7 + 1 = 88$ numbers.

questions.skill: How many numbers in a list
questions.stem: How many numbers are in the list 4, 7, 10, and so on up to 100, where each number is 3 more than the one before?
questions.solution: There are $(100 - 4) \div 3 = 32$ steps of 3, which means 33 numbers.

questions.skill: How many numbers in a list
questions.stem: How many multiples of 5 are there from 1 to 100?
questions.solution: The multiples are $5 \times 1$ up to $5 \times 20$. That is 20 numbers.

questions.skill: How many numbers in a list
questions.stem: How many odd numbers are there from 31 to 79, counting both ends?
questions.solution: The odd numbers go up by 2 each time: $(79 - 31) \div 2 = 24$ steps, so 25 numbers.

questions.skill: How many numbers in a list
questions.stem: The pages of a workbook are numbered from 46 through 123. How many pages is that?

questions.skill: How many numbers in a list
questions.stem: How many numbers are in the list 12, 16, 20, and so on up to 60?
questions.solution: Each number is 4 more than the last. $(60 - 12) \div 4 = 12$ steps, so 13 numbers.

questions.skill: How many numbers in a list
questions.stem: A bus leaves at 8:00 and then every 20 minutes after that. The last bus leaves at 11:00. How many buses leave in all?
questions.solution: From 8:00 to 11:00 is 180 minutes, which is 9 gaps of 20 minutes. Count the first bus too: 10 buses.

questions.stem: A meal is made by choosing 1 of 3 soups, 1 of 4 main dishes and 1 of 2 desserts. How many different meals are there?
questions.solution: Multiply the choices: $3 \times 4 \times 2 = 24$ meals.

questions.stem: A bike lock has 3 wheels, and each wheel shows a digit from 0 to 9. How many different codes can the lock have?
questions.solution: Each wheel has 10 choices: $10 \times 10 \times 10 = 1000$ codes (000 to 999).

questions.stem: A name tag has one letter from A to E followed by one digit from 1 to 9. How many different name tags are possible?
questions.solution: 5 letters and 9 digits: $5 \times 9 = 45$ name tags.

questions.stem: A sandwich has 1 of 2 breads and 1 of 5 fillings, and it may have cheese or not. How many different sandwiches can be made?
questions.solution: Bread: 2 choices. Filling: 5. Cheese: yes or no, 2. So $2 \times 5 \times 2 = 20$ sandwiches.

questions.stem: Kim has 4 shirts and 3 pairs of pants. She may wear one of 2 hats or no hat at all. How many different outfits can she make?
questions.solution: The hat part has 3 choices: either hat, or none. $4 \times 3 \times 3 = 36$ outfits.

questions.stem: How many 3-digit numbers have only odd digits? A digit may be used more than once.
questions.solution: The odd digits are 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, so each of the 3 places has 5 choices: $5 \times 5 \times 5 = 125$.

questions.stem: From home to the park there are 3 paths, from the park to the library 4 paths, and from the library to school 5 paths. How many routes go from home to school through the park and the library?
questions.solution: Multiply the choices at each stage: $3 \times 4 \times 5 = 60$ routes.

questions.stem: Four runners finish a race with no ties. In how many different orders can they finish?
questions.solution: 4 choices for first place, then 3, then 2, then 1: $4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1 = 24$ orders.

questions.stem: How many 3-letter codes can be made from the 5 letters A, B, C, D and E if no letter is used twice?
questions.solution: 5 choices for the first letter, 4 for the second, 3 for the third: $5 \times 4 \times 3 = 60$ codes.

questions.stem: How many 2-digit numbers have two different digits, with both digits chosen from 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5?
questions.solution: 5 choices for the tens digit, then 4 for the ones digit: $5 \times 4 = 20$ numbers.

questions.stem: A code has 3 digits, and each digit is 0, 1 or 2. Digits may repeat. How many codes are there?
questions.solution: Each of the 3 places has 3 choices: $3 \times 3 \times 3 = 27$ codes.

questions.stem: How many 3-digit numbers are there in all, from 100 to 999?
questions.solution: The hundreds digit cannot be 0, so it has 9 choices. The other two digits have 10 choices each: $9 \times 10 \times 10 = 900$.

questions.stem: Each of the digits 1, 2, 3 and 4 is used once to make a 4-digit number. How many of these numbers are even?
questions.solution: The last digit must be 2 or 4: 2 choices. Then the other 3 digits can be placed in $3 \times 2 \times 1 = 6$ ways. So $2 \times 6 = 12$ numbers.

questions.stem: Five people each shake hands once with every other person. How many handshakes are there?
questions.solution: Each of 5 people shakes 4 hands, which is 20, but every handshake is counted twice (once by each person). So $20 \div 2 = 10$ handshakes.

questions.stem: In a class of 20 students, 12 play soccer, 9 play chess and 3 play both. How many students play soccer or chess or both?
questions.solution: The 3 who play both are in each count, so subtract them once: $12 + 9 - 3 = 18$ students.

questions.stem: Of 15 children, 9 like pizza and 8 like pasta. Every child likes at least one of the two. How many like both?
questions.solution: $9 + 8 = 17$ counts the children who like both twice. There are only 15 children, so 2 are counted twice: 2 like both.

questions.stem: How many whole numbers from 1 to 30 are multiples of 2 or multiples of 3?
questions.solution: There are 15 multiples of 2 and 10 multiples of 3. The 5 multiples of 6 are in both lists, so $15 + 10 - 5 = 20$.

questions.stem: Six teams are in a league, and every team plays every other team exactly once. How many games are played?
questions.solution: Each team plays 5 games, and $6 \times 5 = 30$ counts every game twice. So $30 \div 2 = 15$ games.

questions.stem: A book on a shelf is 7th from the left and 9th from the right. How many books are on the shelf?
questions.solution: The book is counted in both numbers, so $7 + 9 - 1 = 15$ books.

questions.stem: How many whole numbers from 1 to 50 have the digit 5 in them?
questions.solution: The numbers are 5, 15, 25, 35, 45 and 50. That is 6 numbers.

questions.stem: How many 3-digit numbers have digits that add up to 4?
questions.solution: Hundreds digit 1: the other two add to 3 (03, 12, 21, 30), 4 numbers. Hundreds digit 2: others add to 2 (02, 11, 20), 3 numbers. Hundreds digit 3: 2 numbers. Hundreds digit 4: 1 number. $4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10$.

questions.stem: How many ways can you make 30 cents using nickels (5 cents), dimes (10 cents) and quarters (25 cents)? You do not have to use every kind of coin, and the order does not matter.
questions.solution: With a quarter: 5 cents left, so 1 nickel (1 way). With no quarter: 0, 1, 2 or 3 dimes, and nickels for the rest (4 ways). Total: 5 ways.

solve.work: With 1 quarter: remaining 5 cents = 1 nickel (1 way). With 0 quarters: 30 cents from dimes and nickels: 0, 1, 2 or 3 dimes, the rest nickels (4 ways). Total 1 + 4 = 5.

questions.stem: A frog climbs 6 stairs, going up 1 or 2 stairs at a time. In how many different ways can it reach the top?
questions.solution: Let the number of ways to reach stair n be the sum of the ways to reach n-1 and n-2. For stairs 1 to 6 this gives 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13. The answer is 13.

questions.stem: Three different numbers from 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 are added to make 10. How many different sets of three numbers can do this? The order does not matter.
questions.solution: The sets are {1, 3, 6}, {1, 4, 5} and {2, 3, 5}. No other set of three different numbers adds up to 10. So 3 sets.

questions.stem: How many different ways can the letters of the word MOM be arranged in a row? Arrangements that look the same when written count once.
questions.solution: The arrangements are MOM, MMO and OMM. Swapping the two Ms gives the same word, so $3 \times 2 \times 1 = 6$ would count each one twice. The answer is 3.

questions.stem: How many 2-digit numbers have a tens digit that is bigger than the ones digit?
questions.solution: Tens digit 1 has 1 choice for the ones digit (0). Tens digit 2 has 2 (0, 1). Tens digit 9 has 9. Total: $1 + 2 + \ldots + 9 = 45$.

solve.work: Tens d gives d choices of ones: 1+2+...+9 = 45.

questions.skill: How many numbers in a list
questions.stem: How many numbers are in the list 5, 12, 19, and so on up to 348, where each number is 7 more than the one before?
questions.solution: $(348 - 5) \div 7 = 49$ steps, so there are 50 numbers.

questions.skill: How many numbers in a list
questions.stem: How many multiples of 7 are there between 100 and 300?
questions.solution: The first multiple is $7 \times 15 = 105$ and the last is $7 \times 42 = 294$. So there are $42 - 15 + 1 = 28$ of them.

questions.skill: How many numbers in a list
questions.stem: The pages of a book are numbered from 1 to 60. How many digits are printed in all to number the pages?
questions.solution: Pages 1 to 9 use 1 digit each: 9 digits. Pages 10 to 60 are 51 pages with 2 digits each: 102 digits. Total: 111.

questions.skill: How many numbers in a list
questions.stem: How many whole numbers from 1 to 100 are NOT multiples of 3?
questions.solution: There are 33 multiples of 3 from 1 to 100 (the last is 99). So $100 - 33 = 67$ are not multiples.

questions.skill: How many numbers in a list
questions.stem: How many 3-digit numbers are multiples of 10?
questions.solution: They are 100, 110, ..., 990, which is $10 \times 10$ up to $10 \times 99$. That is $99 - 10 + 1 = 90$ numbers.

questions.skill: How many numbers in a list
questions.stem: A list starts 100, 97, 94, 91 and keeps going down by 3 until it reaches 10. How many numbers are in the list?
questions.solution: $(100 - 10) \div 3 = 30$ steps, so there are 31 numbers.

questions.stem: How many 3-digit numbers have three different digits?
questions.solution: 9 choices for the hundreds digit (not 0). 9 for the tens digit (any digit but the first). 8 for the ones digit. $9 \times 9 \times 8 = 648$.

questions.stem: A code has 4 digits. The first digit cannot be 0 and the last digit must be even. The two middle digits can be anything from 0 to 9. How many codes are there?
questions.solution: First digit: 9 choices. Middle digits: 10 each. Last digit: 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8, which is 5 choices. $9 \times 10 \times 10 \times 5 = 4500$.

questions.stem: How many even 3-digit numbers are there?
questions.solution: Hundreds digit: 9 choices. Tens digit: 10. Ones digit: 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8, which is 5. $9 \times 10 \times 5 = 450$.

questions.stem: A code is a letter from A to E, then a digit from 0 to 9, then a second letter from A to E that must be different from the first letter. How many codes are there?
questions.solution: 5 choices for the first letter, 10 for the digit, and 4 for the second letter. $5 \times 10 \times 4 = 200$.

questions.stem: A sandwich shop has 3 breads, 5 fillings and 4 sauces. A sandwich has one bread, one filling, and either one sauce or no sauce. How many different sandwiches can be ordered?
questions.solution: The sauce part has 4 + 1 = 5 choices. So $3 \times 5 \times 5 = 75$ sandwiches.

questions.stem: Digits may repeat. How many 2-digit numbers can be made from the digits 0, 1, 2 and 3? A number cannot start with 0.
questions.solution: The tens digit can be 1, 2 or 3: 3 choices. The ones digit can be any of the 4 digits. $3 \times 4 = 12$ numbers.

questions.stem: A flag has 3 stripes in a row, and each stripe is red, white, blue or green. Two stripes next to each other must be different colors. How many different flags can be made?
questions.solution: 4 choices for the first stripe. Each next stripe can be any color except the one before it: 3 choices each. $4 \times 3 \times 3 = 36$ flags.

questions.stem: A club has 6 members. It chooses a president, a vice president and a treasurer, all different people. In how many ways can it do this?
questions.solution: 6 choices for president, 5 for vice president, 4 for treasurer: $6 \times 5 \times 4 = 120$.

questions.stem: Five children line up, and Zoe must be first. In how many ways can the other four children stand behind her?
questions.solution: 4 choices for second place, 3 for third, 2 for fourth, 1 for last: $4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1 = 24$.

questions.stem: Al and Bea are 2 of 4 people who sit in four seats in a row. Al and Bea must sit next to each other. In how many ways can the four people be seated?
questions.solution: Treat Al and Bea as one block. The block and the 2 other people can be ordered in $3 \times 2 \times 1 = 6$ ways. Inside the block, Al and Bea can swap: 2 ways. $6 \times 2 = 12$.

solve.work: Treat Al-Bea as a block: 3! = 6 arrangements x 2 orders = 12.

questions.stem: No digit is used twice. How many 3-digit numbers can be made from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 if the last digit must be 5?
questions.solution: The last digit is 5. The first digit has 4 choices (1 to 4), and the middle digit has 3 left. $4 \times 3 = 12$ numbers.

solve.work: Last is 5; first two from 4 digits: 4x3 = 12.

questions.stem: Each of the digits 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 may be used at most once. How many 4-digit even numbers can be made?
questions.solution: The last digit is 2 or 4: 2 choices. The first digit has 4 choices left, the next 3, the next 2. $2 \times 4 \times 3 \times 2 = 48$.

solve.work: Last digit 2 or 4: 2 ways; first three from remaining 4: 4x3x2 = 24; 48.

questions.stem: A relay team has 4 runners chosen from 6 runners and put in running order. How many different teams can be made, if a different running order counts as a different team?
questions.solution: 6 choices for the first runner, 5 for the second, 4 for the third, 3 for the fourth: $6 \times 5 \times 4 \times 3 = 360$.

questions.stem: Which calculation gives the number of ways to arrange 5 different books in a row on a shelf?
questions.solution: 5 choices for the first spot, 4 for the next, then 3, 2 and 1: $5 \times 4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1 = 120$.

questions.stem: In a group of 30 children, 18 play piano, 15 play violin and 5 play neither. How many play both?
questions.solution: 25 children play at least one instrument. Adding 18 and 15 gives 33, which is 8 too many, because those 8 are counted twice. So 8 play both.

questions.stem: How many whole numbers from 1 to 100 are multiples of 4 or multiples of 6?
questions.solution: 25 multiples of 4, and 16 multiples of 6. Multiples of both 4 and 6 are multiples of 12: 8 of them, counted twice. $25 + 16 - 8 = 33$.

questions.stem: Seven friends each play one chess game against every other friend. How many games are played in all?
questions.solution: Each friend plays 6 games, so $7 \times 6 = 42$, but every game is counted twice. $42 \div 2 = 21$ games.

questions.stem: How many whole numbers from 1 to 60 are multiples of 3 but not multiples of 5?
questions.solution: There are 20 multiples of 3. Of these, the multiples of 15 (15, 30, 45, 60) are also multiples of 5: 4 of them. $20 - 4 = 16$.

questions.stem: All 40 children in a school club take art, music, or both. 25 take art and 22 take music. How many take exactly one of the two?
questions.solution: $25 + 22 = 47$, which is 7 more than 40, so 7 children take both. Exactly one: $40 - 7 = 33$.

questions.stem: How many 2-digit numbers have the digit 7 at least once?
questions.solution: 70 to 79 gives 10 numbers. Numbers ending in 7 with a different tens digit: 17, 27, 37, 47, 57, 67, 87, 97 is 8 more (77 is already counted). Total 18.

questions.stem: How many 3-digit numbers have at least one digit equal to 5?
questions.solution: There are 900 three-digit numbers. Those with no 5 at all: 8 choices for the first digit (not 0 or 5), and 9 choices for each of the other two. $8 \times 9 \times 9 = 648$. So $900 - 648 = 252$.

questions.stem: What is $156 \div 3$?
questions.solution: Split 156 into 150 + 6. Then 150 ÷ 3 = 50 and 6 ÷ 3 = 2, so the answer is 52.

questions.stem: Which number is equal to $84 \div 4$?
questions.solution: 4 goes into 8 two times, and into the 4 left one time, so 84 ÷ 4 = 21. Check: 21 × 4 = 84.

questions.stem: Six children share 96 stickers equally. How many stickers does each child get?
A rope is 252 centimeters long. It is cut into 6 pieces of equal length. How long is each piece, in centimeters?
questions.solution: 25 ÷ 6 is 4 with 1 left over. Bring down the 2 to get 12, and 12 ÷ 6 = 2. So each piece is 42 centimeters.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: $7 \times \square = 91$. What number goes in the blank?
questions.solution: The blank is 91 ÷ 7 = 13. Check: 7 × 13 = 91.

questions.stem: Divide 368 by 4. What do you get?
questions.solution: 36 ÷ 4 = 9, then 8 ÷ 4 = 2. The answer is 92.

questions.stem: What is the remainder when 23 is divided by 5?
questions.solution: 4 × 5 = 20, and 23 − 20 = 3. The remainder is 3.

questions.stem: What is the remainder when 47 is divided by 6?
questions.solution: 7 × 6 = 42 and 47 − 42 = 5. The remainder is 5.

questions.stem: When 59 is divided by 8, the quotient is 7. What is the remainder?
Which division has a remainder of 0?
questions.solution: 9 × 5 = 45, so 45 ÷ 9 has no remainder. The others leave 5, 3 and 3.

questions.stem: Zoe divides 100 by 9. What is the remainder?
Sara has 23 stickers. Each album page holds 5 stickers. How many pages does she need to hold all 23 stickers?
questions.solution: 23 ÷ 5 = 4 with 3 left over. Four pages are full, and the 3 stickers left need one more page. She needs 5 pages.

questions.stem: A baker puts 47 cookies into boxes of 6. How many boxes are completely full?
questions.solution: 47 ÷ 6 = 7 with 5 left over. Seven boxes are full.

questions.stem: A teacher shares 38 pencils equally among 5 students. She gives out as many as she can. How many pencils are left over?
questions.solution: Each student gets 7 pencils, using 35 pencils. 38 − 35 = 3 pencils are left.

questions.stem: A shop packs 50 rolls into bags of 8. Bags are filled one at a time. How many rolls are left over?
questions.solution: 6 bags use 6 × 8 = 48 rolls. 50 − 48 = 2 rolls are left over.

questions.stem: A ribbon is 29 centimeters long. Dev cuts as many whole 4-centimeter pieces as he can. How many pieces does he get?
questions.solution: 29 ÷ 4 = 7 with 1 left over. He gets 7 whole pieces.

questions.stem: One taxi holds 4 people. Twenty-one people need a ride. How many taxis are needed?
questions.solution: 21 ÷ 4 = 5 with 1 left over. Five taxis hold 20 people, so the last person needs a sixth taxi.

questions.stem: What is $4{,}500 \div 10$?
questions.solution: Dividing by 10 takes one zero off the end: 4,500 ÷ 10 = 450.

questions.stem: Which number is equal to $240 \div 40$?

questions.solution: The greatest remainder when dividing by 8 is 7. So the number is 12 × 8 + 7 = 96 + 7 = 103.

questions.solution: The numbers are 2, 9, 16, ..., 100, each 7 more than the one before. From 2 to 100 is 98, and 98 ÷ 7 = 14 steps. That makes 14 + 1 = 15 numbers.

questions.solution: 13 × 500 = 6,500, leaving 500. 13 × 38 = 494, leaving 6. So the remainder is 6.

questions.stem: A group of 100 people rides in vans. Each van holds 8 people. The vans are filled one at a time and the last van carries whoever is left. How many people ride in the last van?
questions.solution: 12 vans carry 96 people. The other 100 − 96 = 4 people ride in the last van.

questions.stem: Today is Tuesday. What day of the week will it be 100 days from today?
questions.solution: The days repeat every 7. 100 ÷ 7 = 14 with 2 left over. So 100 days is 14 whole weeks (back to Tuesday) plus 2 more days: Thursday.

solve.work: 100 = 14 x 7 + 2: two days after Tuesday is Thursday.

questions.stem: Beads are strung in a repeating pattern: red, blue, green, yellow, red, blue, green, yellow, and so on. What color is the 50th bead?
questions.solution: The pattern repeats every 4 beads. 50 ÷ 4 = 12 with 2 left over. So the 50th bead is the 2nd color of the pattern: blue.

questions.stem: A number is divided by 7. The quotient and the remainder are the same number, and the number is more than 40 and less than 50. What is the number?

solve.work: n = 7q + q = 8q with q <= 6. Between 40 and 50: 48 (q = 6).

questions.stem: What is the smallest number greater than 1 that leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by 2, by 3, by 4, by 5 and by 6?

solve.work: n - 1 is a multiple of lcm(2,3,4,5,6) = 60; smallest n > 1 is 61.

questions.stem: Tara always lies. She says: "I have 3 dogs." Tara has either 3 dogs or 4 dogs. How many dogs does she have?

questions.stem: Dan always tells the truth. Zack always lies. Both are asked: "Is 9 an even number?" How many of them answer "yes"?

questions.stem: Eli always tells the truth. He says: "The pet is not a cat, and it is not a bird." The pet is a cat, a bird or a fish. Which is it?
questions.solution: Eli tells the truth, so the pet is not a cat and not a bird. The only one left is a fish.

solve.work: Not a cat, not a bird: a fish.

questions.stem: Ari always tells the truth and Bo always lies. One of them has the key. Ari says: "Bo has the key." Bo says: "I do not have the key." Who has the key?

solve.work: Ari is truthful: Bo has the key. Bo's denial is a lie, consistent.

questions.stem: Of three children, exactly one always tells the truth and two always lie. Ana says: "Ben is the truth-teller." Ben says: "I am the truth-teller." Cora says: "Ana is a liar." Who is the truth-teller?
questions.solution: Try Ana as the truth-teller: she says Ben is, which would make two truth-tellers. No. Try Ben: then Ana would be a liar saying something true. solve.work: Ana truthful -> Ben too (two truth-tellers), no. Ben truthful -> Ana's statement true, but she must lie, no. Cora truthful: Ana liar (says Ben, false), Ben liar (false claim). Cora.

questions.stem: Dan always tells the truth. Dan says: "Eve and I are both truth-tellers." What is Eve? (A truth-teller always tells the truth. A liar always lies.)
questions.solution: Dan tells the truth, so what he said is true: Eve and Dan are both truth-tellers.

solve.work: Dan's statement is true, so Eve is a truth-teller.

questions.stem: Fay always lies. Fay says: "Gus and I are both liars." What is Gus? (A truth-teller always tells the truth. A liar always lies.)
questions.solution: Fay is a liar, so what she said is false. "Gus and I are both liars" would be true only if Gus were a liar too (Fay is one). Since it is false, Gus is not a liar. So Gus is a truth-teller.

solve.work: The statement is false; Fay is a liar, so Gus is not a liar: truth-teller.

questions.stem: Each of Ann, Bo and Cy is a truth-teller or a liar. Ann says: "Bo is a liar." Bo says: "Cy is a liar." Cy says: "Ann and Bo are both liars." How many of the three are liars? (A truth-teller always tells the truth. A liar always lies.)
questions.solution: If Cy told the truth, Ann and Bo would both be liars. But then Ann would be a liar saying "Bo is a liar", which is true. That cannot happen. So Cy is a liar. Then "Cy is a liar" is true, so Bo is a truth-teller. Then "Bo is a liar" is false, so Ann is a liar. Liars: Ann and Cy, which is 2.

solve.work: Ann T -> Bo L -> Cy T -> 'Ann and Bo both liars' false, contradiction. Ann L -> Bo T -> Cy L; Cy's claim false (Bo T), Ann's claim false. Liars: Ann, Cy = 2.

questions.stem: Four people each say one thing. Ann: "Exactly one of us is a liar." Ben: "Exactly two of us are liars." Cat: "Exactly three of us are liars." Dan: "All four of us are liars." How many of them are liars? (A truth-teller always tells the truth. A liar always lies.)

solve.work: Claims exclude each other, at most one true. None true means all 4 liars, making Dan's true: no. One true -> 3 liars -> Cat's claim true, consistent. 3.

questions.stem: Sue says: "Tom is a truth-teller." Tom says: "Sue and I are different: one of us is a truth-teller and the other is a liar." How many of the two are liars? (A truth-teller always tells the truth. A liar always lies.)

Then Tom is not a truth-teller, so he is a liar too. Check: both are liars, so Tom's statement "we are different" is false, as it should be. Two liars.

Each is a truth-teller or a liar, and exactly one of them is a truth-teller. Who is it? (A truth-teller always tells the truth. A liar always lies.)
questions.solution: Try each one as the only truth-teller. If Max is, then Nia and Ola are both liars, so Max is right. But Nia, a liar, says "Ola is a liar", which is true. That fails. If Ola is, then Ola's statement "Max is a truth-teller" would be true, making two truth-tellers. That fails. If Nia is, then Max and Ola are liars. Nia says "Ola is a liar", which is true. Ola says "Max is a truth-teller", which is false. Max says that Nia and Ola are the same kind, which is false because Nia is a truth-teller and Ola is a liar. Everything fits, so Nia.

solve.work: Max T -> Nia, Ola both liars -> Nia's 'Ola is a liar' true, contradiction. Ola T -> Max T, two truth-tellers. Nia T: Ola L, Max L (Nia, Ola differ, his claim false), Ola's claim false. Nia.

solve.work: Truth days Thu-Sun; yesterday a lying day (Mon-Wed) means today is Tue-Thu. Thursday.

questions.stem: Cal always lies. He says three things: "My number is even." "My number is bigger than 10." "My number is a multiple of 3." Cal's number is a whole number from 1 to 20. What is the sum of all the numbers it could be?

questions.stem: Six people stand in a row. The first says: "At least 1 of us is a liar." The second says: "At least 2 of us are liars." The third says "At least 3 of us are liars", and so on, until the sixth says: "At least 6 of us are liars." Each is a truth-teller or a liar. How many are liars? (A truth-teller always tells the truth. A liar always lies.)
questions.solution: If there are L liars, the statements "at least 1", ..., "at least L" are true, and the later ones are false. So the first L people tell the truth and the other 6 - L are liars. The number of liars is L, so 6 - L = L, and L = 3.

solve.work: With L liars, claims 1..L are true, so truth-tellers = L and liars = 6 - L. L = 3.

questions.stem: Three people are each a truth-teller or a liar. Axel says: "Exactly two of us are liars." Bree says: "Exactly one of us is a liar." Cole says: "Axel and Bree are both liars." Who is the only truth-teller? (A truth-teller always tells the truth. A liar always lies.)
questions.solution: Axel and Bree cannot both be truthful, since their statements disagree. Try Axel truthful: then exactly two are liars, so Bree and Cole lie. Check: Bree's "exactly one liar" is false, which fits a liar. Cole's "Axel and Bree are both liars" is false because Axel is truthful, which also fits. Now try Bree truthful: then exactly one is a liar, so Axel is the liar and Cole is truthful, but Cole says Bree is a liar, which is false. That fails. And if nobody is truthful, all three are liars, but then Cole's statement "Axel and Bree are both liars" would be true. That fails too. So the only truth-teller is Axel.

solve.work: Axel T: Bree, Cole liars; Bree's claim false, Cole's false. Consistent. Bree T forces Cole T, whose claim is then false; Cole T makes Axel's claim true. Axel.

questions.solution: If Ann is a truth-teller, Ben is a liar, so Cat is a truth-teller (Ben's statement is false), so Dan is a liar, and Dan's statement "Ann is a liar" is false, which fits. If Ann is a liar, we get the opposite pattern. Either way the types alternate, so 2 are liars.

solve.work: Types must alternate around the table (T L T L or L T L T). Both give 2 liars.
